commit.message:
feat(viewport): orthographic projection mode - browser radios and bare P flip it

- `Camera` grows a `projection: ProjectionMode` field (Perspective stays
  the default). The mode rides the camera itself, so `mvp`, `ray_through`
  and `dolly_cursor` share one decision by construction and every
  existing `mvp(aspect)` call site keeps working untouched. `frame`,
  `toward` and `oriented` carry it; orbit, pan and zoom leave it alone.
- Ortho branch: an affine matrix (clip.w is 1, linear depth), view
  half-height `dist * tan(30 deg)` - exactly the height perspective
  sees at the target plane - so the mode switch never jumps the framing
  and `dist` keeps spelling zoom for orbit, pan and frame alike. Pick
  rays go parallel through the same matrix, and the ortho dolly holds
  the world point under the cursor.
- It is ephemeral view state, like the Solids radios: a direct field
  flip through `actions::toggle_projection`, never a command, never
  saved in the project; the sim's `PreviewCamera` stays perspective.
- UI: a Projection radio row (Perspective / Ortho) under the Solids
  radios in the browser pane, and bare P in `shortcuts()` toggles it
  with the same guard as bare F, so Ctrl+P keeps its post dialog and
  the Alt lanes stay clear.

Pins: `projection_tests` in law_tests - the matrix is affine where
perspective is not, ortho rays are parallel and the cursor closes
through the matrix, sizes ignore depth where perspective shrinks them,
the mode switch agrees at the target plane, the ortho dolly holds the
cursor point, and the camera transforms carry the mode. In the egui
shell: `projection_radios_flip_the_viewport_mode` (real pointer
events, queues nothing) and `bare_p_flips_projection_without_a_command`
(P toggles, Ctrl+P still arms PostProgramDialog). Snapshots rebuilt
for the new browser row.

Fixes #434

fix(post): built-in VMC and tilt-head stroke bands in program coordinates

The VMC 3-axis (vmc.mch) and tilt-head (tilthead.mch) stated their
machine-frame strokes (Z -500..0, X +/-300, Y +/-250), but the limit
checker reads travel in program coordinates through the work offset.
Every move above the Z0 work origin - every retract and clearance -
was out of stroke, so no program posted on the built-in VMC.

Restate both files the way the Tormach files already are: a stroke L
is -L..L (the work origin may sit anywhere along the slide). Z is now
-500..500, X -600..600, Y -500..500. The rule is spelled out in the
app::machine module doc and assets/machines/AGENTS.md. A program that
reaches past L from its own origin still refuses by name.

Pinned by vmc_stroke: a plate contour on the built-in VMC passes the
gate and posts; a Z 520 clearance is refused naming Z and the stroke.

fix(sim): judge a gouge with tol of lateral slack at a wall

The program sim's gouge verdict (column engine `deviate` and field arm
`deviate_field`) charged a column by height alone at its centre. A
height verdict's normal-distance tolerance is tol*cos(slope), zero at a
vertical wall, so a column centre microns inside a wall, reached by a
tool finishing that wall within tolerance, read as a gouge the wall's
whole height and the post gate refused a correct program.

A gouge candidate is now judged against the lowest part top within tol
of its centre (centre plus an eight-direction ring at radius tol; air
counts as lowest), in the new `stock_sim::wall_slack`, shared by both
engines. A column past the slack still convicts at its centre's depth;
rest is unchanged; a clean program pays nothing extra.

On the user's Milling-test.step: a 3D Finish (BN-0600) on model stock
was refused for 10.21 mm at (16.69, -24.91), a column 1-3 um inside the
D's wall; in the 70x70x27 box stock for 37 cells, worst 22.01 mm. Both

fix(sim): fixture laws pad an arc's chords by its bulge

The box fixture laws (c2)/(d2) swept an arc along its inscribed chords
(Move::segments3 at the chord tolerance) with each band's bare radius.
The circle bulges past every chord by up to its sagitta, so steel in
that sliver went unseen. Measured: an R30 arc with an r3 flute, where the
box face sat half a sagitta inside the true reach, reported no FixtureHit.

The new sim::verify::arc_bulge bounds how far the true path can stand
off each chord: the sagitta r(1 - cos psi) across it and r(psi - sin psi)
along it (fraction-matched, psi <= pi/2; 2r over a half turn), plus
ARC_PAD = 1 um for the lattice-snapped centre.

- stack_span::pieces/band_struck: every arc piece pads the band radius
  (upright column and lean enclosure). In XY the pad is the whole
  deviation. In XZ/YZ it is only the horizontal part. A vertical arc's
  z window is its true z range between joints (joints for Z-monotone
  pieces, carried to the circle's extremum for an unsplit arc), so a
  lead arc landing tangent on a mounting face stays flush and silent.
- posed_steel: an arc move's capsules grow by the 3-D deviation.
- Straight moves pad nothing, so their verdicts are byte-identical. An
  arc with a non-finite centre or radius fails closed.

commit.message:
fix(sim): judge spindle-C moves at the station pose and fixed steel in the machine frame

Reproduced first: on main the box fixture laws missed real hits under
the spindle C. Fixed steel was read in the part frame (the machine-frame
sweep cannot stand a radial pose upright about a vertical line, so the
part-frame verdict stood), so steel at the live-tool station was seen
only near C 0 - a generated Rotary Contour on a mill-turn C passed a
fixed steady at the station silent on the far side of the bar. Steel
riding the part was read at the whole move's pose, because cl::stamp_c
gave every piece the move's end axis.

- cl::stamp_c: each piece states the station pose at its own C (the
  move's axis turned by the turn left; the last piece bit-identical).
  The post writes C only, so the stream and goldens are unchanged.
- sim::verify::c_steel (new): the workholding laws read a C move's pose
  from its C (also keeps pre-fix cached paths honest), and read fixed
  steel in the machine frame too - the tip straight on the station ray,
  pose +X - adding hits to the part-frame verdict, never removing one.
  The spindle line is recovered from the stamped tips, else the op's
  axis, and used only when every tip agrees; otherwise a C move against
  fixed steel fails closed.

Pinned by crates/sim/tests/c_axis_fixture.rs and
crates/app/tests/c_axis_fixture.rs (both fail on main). No existing
verdict changed.

fix(app): a typed Slot's caps no longer read as a gouge

The stadium a Slot is verified against drew each round end as 16 chords
inscribed in the true arc, up to h(1 - cos 5.625 deg) inside it: for a
6 mm cutter on a 6 mm slot the cap-centre position read 2.9855 mm from
the boundary against the gouge law's r - tol = 2.99, so every plunge and
feed of a slot whose cutter reaches its end was a Gouge and never posted.

The caps are now the polygon circumscribed about the arc (tangent
chords, corners at h / cos(phi/2)), with the chord count chosen so a
corner stands at most 1 um outside the arc. A tangent cutter verifies
clean; a 0.05 mm over-cut of the cap still convicts. GOUGE_TOL is
unchanged and the posted G-code does not change.

Fixes #510

feat(post): optionally end a Tormach program in the machine's native units

LinuxCNC's M2/M30 reset list (linuxcnc.org/docs, M-codes, "M2, M30
Program End") does not include G20/G21, so a mm program leaves an
inch-run PathPilot control in mm after M30. A new post option, "End in"
(Program's unit by default / Inch / mm), lives in PostOptions as
end_units. It is set through the undoable SetPostOptions, saved as
post_options.end_units (additive, no version step), and reaches the
script as postOptions.EndUnits. When the chosen unit differs from the
